issues.title: [Bug]: aggregated variable accepted outside an aggregated-variable-reference
issues.output:
Compiles and runs without diagnostics; prints:
3
[12,13,14]
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main 00d6965: the program compiles and prints 3 and [12,13,14]. A clean-context spec check (2024R1 spec §6.35.7, §6.9) found that aggregated variables (y from collect, n2 after group by) may be referenced only through an aggregated-variable-reference, which is a spread-list-member or a rest-arg. So y.length(), n2[0] and n2.length() must be rejected as semantic errors. The front end's semantic checker accepts an invalid program, so this is frontend. It is not a crash. There is no duplicate: #1068 (a valid rest-arg use is rejected) and #1225 (re-aggregation flattens or panics) are related aggregated-variable bugs with different symptoms, and neither is a natural parent.

notes: Only #1440 is new or updated since the 2026-10-26 report. #1423-1425 were triaged in 2026-10-26.json. #1304 and #1282 are still undetermined from 2026-10-20.json and have had no updates. Related issues: #1068, #1225. The search/issues REST endpoint is blocked by the session proxy, so duplicate search used a title scan of all issues.
